About these exercises

The five training sections contain original note arrangements and instructions built around common singing tasks. They are not song transcriptions or reproductions of a named teaching program.

Each section offers a practice focus, not a test of your register. A piano cannot confirm whether you are using chest voice, mix, head voice or falsetto. These labels can also be used differently by different teachers.

Choose a comfortable range before playing. The Baritone and Tenor presets are broad pitch limits, not targets you must reach in every exercise. For chest voice and belt foundations, begin with a small range near comfortable speaking pitch. Adjust the limits whenever the sound stops feeling easy.

Belting exercises here introduce clear, speech-like sounds at moderate volume. They do not teach full-power or high belting on their own. A qualified singing teacher can give feedback on that coordination.

Breathe whenever you need to, even if the piano continues. Hold key repeats a key, not your breath. Use More options to add breathing time. Stop for pain, strain or increasing hoarseness. Persistent symptoms need professional assessment.

Technique references

The general exercise types were checked against these educational resources. The pitch arrangements and short prompts in this app were written for this app. These sources do not endorse the app.

  • Duke Voice Care Center: Ideas for Vocal Exercises
  • NATS: Music Theater Resources
  • ASHA: Voice Disorders, including semi-occluded vocal exercises

This is a practice tool, not voice therapy.
